children: Iceland’s seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose to 6.8% in August 2026, the highest level since February, following an upwardly revised 6.6% in July.
The number of unemployed persons increased by 0.7 thousand month-on-month to 15.9 thousand, including 10.9 thousand men and 5.0 thousand women.
The youth unemployment rate, which measures job-seekers between 16 and 24 years old, climbed to 14.2% from 6.7%, reaching its highest level since May.
Meanwhile, the employment rate edged up to 73.7% from 73.5% in July, with the number of employed individuals rising by 1.2 thousand to 217.8 thousand.
The labor force participation rate ticked higher to 79.0% from 78.7%.
On a non-seasonally adjusted basis, the unemployment rate rose to 6.0% in August from 5.5% in the previous month.

title: Iceland Jobless Rate Rises to 6-Month High
